attrs.why: Current frontier is 'Macular tractional lesion' (node-5, score 0.8), which is a broad tractional category. OCT evidence (node-9) explicitly shows an epiretinal membrane, a common cause of tractional macular lesions that matches the vascular distortion and hyperreflective mass. This candidate refines the frontier by specifying the tractional element as epiretinal membrane, supported by node-9 and node-4.

Current frontier is 'Macular tractional lesion'. Vitreomacular traction is a specific tractional disorder where the vitreous adheres to the macula and causes traction. OCT findings of disorganized retinal layers and vascular distortion (node-9, node-10) support a tractional process, but no explicit vitreous attachment is described, so confidence is lower than epiretinal membrane.

Current frontier is 'Macular tractional lesion'. An elevated white-greyish macular lesion with vascular distortion (node-4) could represent a tractional retinal detachment. However, no explicit detachment is noted on OCT or FA (node-9, node-10), so this is a less likely refinement.

attrs.why: The radiologist explicitly favors epiretinal membrane-induced right macular traction as the leading diagnosis; OCT directly documents an epiretinal membrane with disorganized retinal layers and a hyperreflective mass, and FA shows tortuosity/leakage consistent with the observed vascular distortion. With this expert support the specific epiretinal-membrane mechanism becomes more likely, raising confidence from 0.8 to 0.85.

node-19.label: Combined hamartoma of the retina and retinal pigment epithelium

attrs.why: The elevated white-greyish macular lesion with vascular distortion, together with the epiretinal membrane and hyperreflective mass on OCT, matches the morphology of a combined hamartoma of the retina and retinal pigment epithelium, a benign mass-like lesion that produces traction and vascular tortuosity in young patients. However, no B-scan or histology confirms it and the radiologist favors a primary epiretinal membrane, so confidence is moderate (0.35).

node-20.label: Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome (Gorlin syndrome)

attrs.why: Multiple odontogenic cysts, macrocephaly, scoliosis, and a maternal history of skin cancer and maxillary cysts closely match nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome (Gorlin syndrome), which features odontogenic keratocysts, macrocephaly, scoliosis, and basal cell carcinomas. Genetic testing and brain MRI are not yet available and no direct link to the eye lesion is established, so confidence is moderate (0.4).
